QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_48

question.text: In the equity derivative market, what does MWPL (Market Wide Position Limit) refer to?

answer.text: The market-wide open-interest limit on F&O contracts in an individual security, set at 20% of the non-promoter/free-float shares and monitored across exchanges
The maximum amount a single trader can invest in the stock market
The daily trading volume limit set by SEBI for each stock
The maximum number of stocks that can be included in a market index

explanation.text: The Logic: MWPL for futures and options on individual securities is set at 20% of the shares held by non-promoters (the free float) in the underlying. Aggregate open interest in F&O contracts on that security is monitored across exchanges against this limit. The Trap: MWPL is not an individual trader cap (those are client-level position limits) and it is not a daily volume ceiling. It is a free-float-based limit on aggregate open interest. Note: When the aggregate open interest in a security's F&O contracts approaches the MWPL threshold, trading restrictions are triggered to keep market-wide positions within the prescribed limit.
